question: Where a package outside this repository's catalogue answers the same job question as one of the operation-scope roles (#505's original six: controller, inspector, builder, locksmith, integrator, observer -- plus architect, added to the decided scope before this ruling) or the interaction-scope roles (#511's original four: bouncer, butler, giver, keeper -- plus messenger, added to the decided scope before this ruling), is the @clossys package authoritative, or does the incumbent win -- and how is that classification made per role, per consuming repository?
options: Every dependency block is parsed structurally (including overrides/resolutions) per role per consuming repository; classify each overlap as 'competitor' (a second answer to the same job question -- the @clossys package is authoritative, and docs/LIFECYCLE.md's 'adopted' bar requires the competitor's removal or narrowing) or 'substrate' (a provider/SDK/service/tool the role gates or reconciles against, not a second answer -- it stays, and the cell remains adoptable).
Assume no overlap without measuring (the status quo before #505/#511 were filed) and let 'adopted' be claimed on installation and wiring alone.
Defer the question indefinitely and block no adoption claim on it.
recommendation: Option 1 -- measure per role, per consuming repository, and classify each overlap as competitor or substrate rather than assuming either 0-of-N or N-of-N overlap. Recommended explicitly, in the same terms, in the Opus scoping recommendation at #1187 comment 5800189482 ('Decision 2'): a flat 'ours is authoritative' statement would wrongly declare the @clossys package authoritative over the very substrates several of these roles read, gate, or reconcile against (a secrets store for locksmith, a CI provider's run history for observer, an identity SDK for bouncer, and so on), so the decision has to carry the competitor/substrate distinction rather than a single blanket rule.
decision: Posted directly on both #511 (comment 5800368649) and #505 (comment 5800368286) as "Owner decision: authority for the operation and interaction roles (2026-09-23)": a competitor is authoritative for the @clossys package and must be removed or narrowed before a cell reads 'adopted'; a substrate stays and the cell remains adoptable. Classification is made per role, per consuming repository, by the job-question test in #511, with dependency blocks parsed structurally, including overrides and resolutions. A contested classification leaves the cell not adopted until the owner rules; a declared non-adoption with a reason remains a legitimate answer, an empty cell does not. Scope: controller, architect, inspector, builder, locksmith, integrator, observer, bouncer, butler, messenger, giver, keeper. This is a rule, not a measurement -- #505's question 1 (does anything already installed cover this role's job?) has never been run; agents may now run that per-repository measurement and declaration work. Revisit if that measurement finds incumbents with broader coverage than the role: clause 1's default then flips back to the 2026-09-16 rule, under which the consumer decides and declares.
notes: Supersedes governance/decisions/operation-interaction-role-authority.json, which sourced the owner's decision only from GitHub comments posted on #511 (5800368649) and #505 (5800368286) -- under the escalation rule (governance/decisions/hitl-escalation-rule.json, Accepted item 1), a GitHub comment posted under this repository's shared agent identity is never proof of owner intent, so that record could not stand as one on its own. RE-CONFIRMED in the coordinator chat on 2026-09-23. The coordinator's message, quoted verbatim: "your earlier decision on operation and interaction role authority (#505/#511) was recorded only from GitHub comments. Under your rule, that record doesn't prove the decision was yours. If you re-confirm it here, it becomes a valid record. … My recommendation is to re-confirm it". The owner quoted "re-confirm" and replied "yes". `question`, `options`, `recommendation`, `decision`, `reviews`, and `links` above are carried forward UNCHANGED from the original record -- the owner re-confirmed the same decision, not a different one; only its channel of record changed. `decision` above therefore still describes itself in the past tense as "Posted directly on both #511 ... and #505 ..." -- that sentence is quoting the ORIGINAL record's own account of how the ruling was first written down, left intentionally untouched per the instruction to keep the decision content unchanged; this record's OWN channel of authority is owner-chat, not that GitHub posting, exactly as this `notes` field states. channel: owner-chat, not independently verifiable (the ratified text's own required disclosure, "Where I'm pushing back" > hardware-signed commits).
